articles.title: New Batman: Part 2 Set Photos Hint at the Court of Owls
articles.summary: New videos and photos from the London set of The Batman: Part II will only fuel the rumors that Gotham’s secret cabal of wealthy elites, the Court of Owls, factor into the movie.
articles.body:
New videos and photos from the London set of The Batman: Part II show Robert Pattinson’s Bruce Wayne being escorted by police through a crowd of angry protestors .

These images only further fuel the rumors that Gotham’s secret cabal of wealthy elites, the Court of Owls , factor into the story, but these photos also hint at another Bat-villain possibly being involved.

NEW LOOK at Robert Pattinson as Bruce Wayne entering a car after going through a crowd of protesters on the set of ‘THE BATMAN: PART 2’ 🦇🔥 (via londonmoviesets | TikTok) pic.twitter.com/w4RA6AZsa5 — The Batman Saga News (@TheBatmanSagaNW) September 13, 2026

NEW LOOK at Robert Pattinson as Bruce Wayne entering a car after going through a crowd of protesters on the set of ‘THE BATMAN: PART 2’ 🦇🔥 (via londonmoviesets | TikTok) pic.twitter.com/w4RA6AZsa5

The signs and placards waved by the protestors’ reveal the source of their anger and the first hint of the Court of Owls: “ Court of Oligarchs ,” “Court of Fouls,” “The Richer Get Richer,” “One Day The Poor Will Have Nothing ,” “ Re$i$t,” “Eat the Rich ,” “Your Greed is Killin Us,” and “Oligarchs Gotta Go!.”

There are also signs bearing Batman imagery, such as one that reads “ Save Us ” and another that features the Batman mask with “I’m coming for you next” written below it.

The irony in these images, of course, is that the protesters clearly view Bruce Wayne, the city’s wealthiest man, as an enemy while embracing his alter ego Batman as a symbol of resistance against a corrupt system.

Most curiously, some protestors are wearing white masks that fully hide their faces . There is one particular masked protester with a white anarchy symbol drawn on his jacket, a look reminiscent of the villain Anarky in the game Batman: Arkham Origins . Might these masked protesters be his henchmen?

In the DC Comics, Anarky is Batman’s most political adversary who uses violence against state and corporate institutions in a quest for social justice. Born Lonnie Machin, he is also one of Batman’s youngest opponents and has sometimes been portrayed as an antihero rather than an outright villain.

A protester with an A symbol on their jacket wearing a white face mask was spotted on the set of ‘THE BATMAN: PART 2’. Anarky? (via @RayChand006 ) pic.twitter.com/18px5FXJKq — The Batman Saga News (@TheBatmanSagaNW) September 13, 2026

A protester with an A symbol on their jacket wearing a white face mask was spotted on the set of ‘THE BATMAN: PART 2’. Anarky? (via @RayChand006 ) pic.twitter.com/18px5FXJKq

Although Anarky has been featured in both live-action (Arrow) and animation (Beware the Batman), he’s never appeared in a Batman feature film. It should be noted that Matt Reeves has said the villain of The Batman: Part II has “ never really been done in a movie before .”

Or maybe that set photo is just of some random extra with an anarchy symbol on his chest and it isn’t a hint at Anarky or his movement being a part of this movie at all. I’m just speculating.

That said, a story featuring both the Court of Owls and Anarky actually makes sense for a Matt Reeves Batman movie where Gotham’s pervasive corruption is front and center.

articles.title: Lanterns Delivers Another Banger in Episode 5 as the Show's 2016 Storyline Reaches a Dramatic Climax
articles.summary: Lanterns wraps up its 2016 storyline with a real bang, as the situation in Rushville devolves into all-out war. Read our full review of Episode 5.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 5!

Lanterns is clearly a show intended to downplay some of the more ostentatious trappings of the source material, both for practical, budgetary reasons and out of a desire to tell a very specific kind of sci-fi detective story. This is not a series where Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart are pulling out their rings and going hogwild with the energy constructs every few minutes. At most, you have to assume the people in charge are saving those flashier, more expensive scenes for a very specific time and place. Well, Episode 5 is that place, and it’s a wild ride.

As Laura Linney’s Lianna describes it, “Lights Out” is a real “shitstorm” moment for the series. This is the episode where the 2016 storyline reaches its grand climax and everything goes to hell for Hal and John. There’s plenty of action to go around this week, which should assuage some of the complaints about the series holding back on Green Lantern constructs and general superheroics. Granted, Hal still doesn’t get overly creative with his ring-slinging (it’s mostly shields and generic energy blasts here), but the larger scale of Episode 5 is definitely appreciated.

More than the epic shootouts and battle scenes, however, it’s really the tension and character conflicts that fuel “Lights Out.” After weeks of watching Hal and John slowly come to terms with one another, it’s quite a change to see that relationship fall apart and watch as the two characters find themselves on opposite sides of the battle currently tearing Rushville apart. John chose to put his faith in Hal, just as Hal himself decided that John is a pawn worth sacrificing in his bid to remain Green Lantern of Sector 2814.

Addressing that particular elephant in the room, I can easily see this episode sticking in the craw of a great many Hal Jordan fans. Even for those willing to tolerate the notion of Hal being painted as a massive jerk of questionable morals, seeing him outright betray John and leave him for dead, and then orchestrate a massacre for his personal benefit may be a bridge too far. I get it. There’s only one specific storyline from the comics where Hal has this much blood on his hands (1994’s “Emerald Twilight”), and even there, he had the excuse of being driven temporarily insane (not to mention that DC has made a point of absolving Hal of his actions in the decades since).

But I’m still willing to roll with this particular interpretation of Hal Jordan. Clearly, there’s something fundamentally broken inside of this character. The interaction between Hal and the Halogram highlights that fact well (kudos to Chandler for pulling off those scenes so adeptly). This very dated copy of Hal is a nicer and more fundamentally decent version of the man, so what exactly transpired in the years since? How bad was that fallout with Sinestro? Hopefully, these are questions the series will explore in the remaining three episodes of the season. Any excuse to get more of Ulrich Thomsen’s Sinestro in the mix.

Episode 5 is also great about fleshing out Zoe (Poorna Jagannathan) and exploring the hold she has over Rushville. As Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) explains, it’s not that she uses her power and resources to rule over the residents of Rushville; she truly is their benefactor and protector. This episode builds an appreciation for the community Zoe has singlehandedly built around herself and how tragic it is that the Lanterns have come calling and blown her cover. I’m also intrigued by the interaction between Zoe and her grandson, Noah (Cary Christopher). She urges him to “Remember everything I told you,” a line that I’m sure will pay off as the series inevitably returns to the 2026 timeline at long last.

There are a couple of quibbles about Episode 5 worth mentioning. I don’t know how non-comic fans may respond to the reveal that the Manhunters were created by the Guardians, but that got a big “No duh!” response from me. I suppose it’s one of those cases where knowing the source material can make the adaptation a little too predictable. More frustrating is that this episode is pretty abrupt in writing Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor) out of the picture. There are some terrific Antaan-centric scenes early on (particularly his showdown with Garret Dillahunt’s Will Macon), but seeing him cavalierly tossed into the sky to self-destruct seems like a less-than-fitting end to the character. At this point, I guess we can cross out that fan theory about Antaan being Atrocitus . At least, I hope we can. The series already wasted Hector Hammond.

Those complaints aside, “Lights Out” serves as a fitting conclusion to the conflict inside Rushville. And nowhere is that more true than with John himself. After being prodded and manipulated and lied to by everyone around him, John is finally forced to choose who and what he stands for. No longer can he be the soldier who blindly follows orders, be those orders from his abusive parents or his superior officers or the self-serving Guardians. The crucible has forged him, only the final product is not a Green Lantern. John emerges on the other side totally disillusioned with the Green Lantern Corps and the ideals they claim to represent. That would certainly explain why he appears to still not be a Lantern in 2026. When the opportunity finally presented itself, John rejected it.

It’s going to be very interesting to see how the series evolves from here. Presumably, the show will finally jump forward to 2026 and pick up where “Pilot” left off. At the same time, there’s a lot of room to look backwards and explore how and why Hal fell so far from grace. Whatever happens, it’s clear we’re looking at a very different show in these next three episodes, and that’s an exciting prospect.

articles.title: The Last of Us Part 2 Multiplayer Mod Cancelled at Sony’s Request
articles.summary: A PvP multiplayer mod for The Last of Us Part 2 on PC is no longer going to be released after the mod maker says it was contacted by Sony Interactive Entertainment and asked not to release the project to the public.
articles.body:
A PvP multiplayer mod for The Last of Us Part 2 on PC is no longer going to be released after the mod maker says it was contacted by Sony Interactive Entertainment and asked not to release the project to the public.

“Hey everyone, as you all know, the TLOU 2 Multiplayer mod that has been in development since January was supposed to [be released] this month,” wrote modder Speclizer via social media. “Unfortunately I recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released. Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day but I hope you’ll continue to follow me onto the next project, this time something of my own.”

Speclizer uploaded 25 minutes of gameplay for the mod back in June, with clarification the project began in January 2026 and was expected to be ready by this month. Development on the mod included a payment component via Patreon, which is unlikely to have helped it fly under the radar.

The news may come as a disappointment to firm fans of The Last of Us multiplayer, considering Naughty Dog cancelled its own official multiplayer project set in the world of The Last of Us back in late 2023. The studio said, if it had released the game as planned, it would have needed to put all of its resources into post-launch content for years to come, harming its ability to develop future single-player games. In the aftermath of the cancellation, former Sony Interactive Entertainment executive Shuhei Yoshida noted that he had played The Last of Us Online and thought it was “great.” The Last of Us Online director Vinit Agarwal also maintains former colleagues still message him to say it was “the best multiplayer game they’ve ever played.”

Luke is a Senior Editor on the IGN reviews team. You can track him down on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

articles.title: The Best Books Of September 2026
articles.summary: From cyberpunk to fantasy and much more, these are our picks for the best new books of the month.
articles.body:
September is shaping up to be one of the best months of the year so far, when it comes to new book releases. With continuations of beloved series, like Leigh Bardugo’s Ninth House Trilogy, L.K. Steven’s Silvercloak Saga, and even Rebecca Yarros’ Threshing Day . And that’s not all.

The upcoming month also sees new stories from some of our favourite authors, including Rachel Harrison, Keith Rosson, Brandon Sanderson and Emily St. John Mandel.

So, if you’re looking to find your next great read, we’ve got you covered, as always.

For fans of Martha Wells’ Murderbot (it’s also giving us big John Wick and Blade Runner vibes, too), you might want to put James Islington’s Scion on your radar this month. Set in a world where the rich – known as lifers – get the opportunity to live forever, as opposed to the poor who die young, Azure is an assassin tasked with killing the richest of them all. That is until he’s hired to protect one of them instead.

Given that this is the exact opposite of what he’s usually tasked with, at just over 200 pages, this is a snappy, fast-paced cyberpunk thriller that you won’t want to put down.

Release date: September 1 (US) and September 8 (UK)

Now, imagine if Groundhog Day was a horror movie, where each iteration of the same day got progressively worse, and you’ve got Rachel Harrison’s incredible new novel, Kiss Slay Replay. And having read an early copy of this myself, I can confidently say that it has easily cemented itself as one of my favourite books of the year.

Set on the day when Willa’s best friends are set to get married, it was always going to be a bittersweet moment, as it sees her come face to face with her ex-fiancé for the first time in months. Oh, and he just so happens to have brought a date to the wedding. If that wasn’t bad enough, something about the day feels off, but Willa can’t quite place it. That is, until a masked killer terrorises the reception, and she certainly doesn’t make it as the final girl. She then wakes up, and it’s the morning of the wedding again. Could it just have been a bad dream? Well, when all manner of horror tropes and terror make their way to the reception day after day, it becomes clear that something is seriously wrong. Stuck in a time loop, she must learn how to escape it or risk being a wedding guest forever.

If you’ve eagerly been anticipating the third and final book in Leigh Bardugo’s brilliant Ninth House trilogy, Dead Beat reunites us with Alex and the delegates of Lethe House. And with the door to hell left open and an increasing number of demons making their way into New Haven and the Yale campus, it will take a herculean effort to stop the gates to the underworld from flooding open permanently.

Thankfully, this isn’t a fight that she will have to face alone. Dawes, Turner, Mercy, and even Tripp will have roles to play, as well as Alex's mentor, Darlington, who is back and cursed with some dangerous powers of his own. Will they be able to stop the onslaught? Or what could go wrong? You’ll need to pick up a copy to find out.

Keith Rosson’s Coffin Moon blew us away last year, so it’s safe to say that we were more than happy to hear that he had a brand new book coming out in 2026. Crone follows ex-detective, ex-addict, and grieving father, Eli, whose daughter disappeared a decade ago. And after spending the ensuing years imploding his life in a bid to find her, or what happened to her, he is now working as an enforcer for a local drug gang to pay off his debt to them.

However, everything changes when the son of his boss is brutally murdered, and he is seemingly given a golden ticket out of his current situation. If he can find out who killed him, his debt will be cleared forever. But all isn’t quite as it seems. With a hunt for answers that brings him face to face with a slew of conspiracy theories and even more tragedies, ones which even reignite those from his own past, something dangerous is lurking in the woods and creeping ever closer.

Release date: September 15 (US) and September 17 (UK)

Emily St. John Mandel’s Station Eleven continues to be one of our favourite post-apocalyptic reads. And she’s back with Exit Party, another immersive story set in a broken world.

The year is 2031, and after America has been at war with itself, things appear to be on the up. The curfew in Los Angeles has been lifted, and the Republic of California has been declared. Finally, there’s some cause for celebration. But, as you might expect in a book like this, the party that our characters find themselves at doesn’t exactly go to plan. And we won’t spoil it beyond that. Years later, living a very different life, one of our main characters continues to be haunted by what happened that night, but could it be the key to a completely different world? If you enjoy Emily St. John Mandel’s distinctive writing, this should definitely be at the top of your TBR (to be read) list this month.

It wouldn’t be a roundup from me without a tiny sprinkling of romance. So, if you’re hoping to read outside of your usual genres this year, or are looking to recommend some new books to family or friends, we always have a lot of fun with B.K. Borison’s books.

Grim Tidings, as you might be able to glean from the title, follows a female Grim Reaper, Darcy, who is tired of shuttling her assignments to the underworld. Upon turning up at Gabriel’s bar, looking for a bit of respite from the day-to-day drudgery of work, they get to talking and sparks fly between the pair. That is until Gabriel discovers what Darcy does for a living. It would probably be alarming for anyone to find out that they’d been flirting with the Grim Reaper, but as the town’s Guardian Angel, he has centuries of bad experiences with Reapers, and surely Darcy is no different. Or is she? Even though this is the second in a series of interconnected stories, you don’t necessarily need to have read Good Spirits to enjoy or jump right into this unique take on a paranormal romance.

Blightfall by Brandon Sanderson and Janci Patterson

Bestselling authors Brandon Sanderson and Janci Patterson have teamed up once again, this time for a new young adult (YA) trilogy set in Sanderson's epic Cytoverse. And after decades of war, Arturo – leader of Skyward Flight – starts to realise that freedom isn’t what he thought it would be.

The threat of the alien oppressors might be over, at least for now, but his first postwar assignment – an attempt to make contact with fellow survivors – is far from simple. With mysterious debris and giant, invasive forests covering most of the planet, Blightfall isn’t exactly hospitable. And when Arturo and his team are attacked, they find themselves trapped there, with no idea who to trust or team up with to make their escape and get home safely.

What would you do if you were being haunted? I’m talking ghosts standing at the end of your bed or appearing when you pull back the shower curtain. And no matter where you go or move to, they follow you there. Well, Jamie thinks that he’s found an ingenious solution when someone is selling their Lion – the world’s most advanced self-driving car. Surely being enclosed and constantly on the move will keep him safe?

If you’ve ever been a bit weary of fully autonomous vehicles, reading this book won’t exactly change your mind, as one morning Jamie wakes up to the Lion speeding down the road. The hood of the car looks to be dented and covered in what appears to be blood, and it won’t respond to his demands or stop to let him out. As they keep driving, Jamie becomes increasingly involved in the car’s decisions, with unimaginable consequences. Published posthumously, following the author’s death in 2025, Driven skillfully blends horror with a type of sci-fi that doesn’t feel all that far away from what could happen now or sometime soon, keeping us firmly in the passenger seat the whole way through.

From the bestselling author of The Fault in Our Stars , Looking for Alaska , and our 2025 top pick Everything Is Tuberculosis , comes John Green’s first novel for adults. And that, in and of itself, immediately piqued our interest. Described as a behind-the-scenes Hollywood love story, it follows rising stars Kai and Juniper, who have just been cast in a biopic that everyone is talking about. And, as is the case for many who find stardom as quickly as this pair do, their lives change in unexpected and unimaginable ways.

Giving us a glimpse into what it takes to make it in the world of Hollywood, as ambition and public attention collide, we get to see the private cost of their public personas. At the same time, it focuses on two young people finding out who they are, both on their own and as a couple. Let’s just say, we can’t wait to curl up with this one soon.

Release date: September 22 (US) and September 24 (UK)

With Halloween and spooky season fast approaching, Jeneva Rose’s trio of eerie short stories is a fantastic way to get in the mood. And the great thing is, each one has its own distinct voice and take on the genre.

First up is ‘Never Kill the Medium,’ which centres around a deadly thirtieth dinner party, where what appeared to be a playful and innocuous séance spirals out of control, with the assembled guests covering up a death and not realising that they’ve left the ritual unfinished. The second story, ‘The Nightmare House,’ is an interesting take on the haunted house story, where a family’s new forever home hides insidious secrets, ones which have seen every family who has lived there either die or disappear. And finally, we have ‘All Curses Are Final,’ as a group of friends stops off at a roadside store. Oh, and there just so happens to be seemingly cursed items for sale there. Good news – the curse is lifted at the time of sale. Bad news – one of the group finds an unpaid item in her bag. Even though she initially laughs it off, things change when they are snowed in at a remote cabin, and things take a turn for the worse.

Book two in the Silvercloak Saga hits shelves this month, and we can’t wait to see where the story goes next. Picking up after the frankly devastating events in Havenwood, Saffron is attempting to move forward and push towards her ultimate revenge. But as she’s still deep undercover in the Bloodmoon gang, she only sees one path forward – to harness her long-dormant Timeweaver power to fix some of her biggest mistakes.

Ordinarily, this would be tricky enough. However, the now kingpin of the gang, Levan, has discovered Saffron’s true identity. And at the same time, an ambitious rookie detective is keen to put a stop to both the Bloodmoons and their rival gangs. How will it all turn out? You’ll need to grab a copy.

Ellis is a freelance journalist, based in the UK, with a love of all things books. She also routinely chairs bookish events up and down the country, getting the scoop from some of the biggest and bestselling authors to keep you in the know.

articles.title: 'They Helped Pay For Our Movie, So Thank You': Marvel's Blade Might Be Scrapped, But Mahershala Ali Says He's Grateful He Got a Year of Free Training
articles.summary: Mahershala Ali has thanked Marvel for a year of free physical training, and said his prep time for the now-cancelled Blade helped pay for his new movie instead.
articles.body:
Mahershala Ali has thanked Marvel for a year of free physical training, and said his prep time for the now-cancelled Blade helped pay for his new movie instead.

Ali is now set to star in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother , an action thriller where he plays a hitman with a baby, written and directed by Bassam Tariq. Ali and Tariq met when the latter was set to direct Marvel's long-awaited Blade, though Tariq later departed the project amid its years of ongoing delays.

With Blade now scrapped, the pair have reteamed for this new action movie, which will finally put Ali's freshly-toned body to good use. And now, Ali has thanked Marvel for his time training to be Blade — saying it had allowed him to step into this project, already fit and ready.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

"It was a little more than a year," Ali said of his time training for Blade, in conversation with Deadline . "And actually I'm really grateful, they helped pay for our movie, so thank you. We wouldn't, we couldn't have afforded to... there's no way we could have [done] this film and I got to go train for a year. So at this point, I'm so grateful that they made a wonderful contribution to our film."

Asked yet again if Marvel's Blade project was dead, Ali replied:

"I'm done. I'm doing this and anything else moving forward. I'm over that, I'm done with that."

Marvel announced it was making Blade back in 2019 at San Diego Comic-Con, and confirmed that Ali would feature as a new version of its vampire hunter, previously played by Wesley Snipes. But, seven years later, the project is dead in the water, despite the previous enthusiasm from Ali to make it.

Back in July, Ali stated that he had moved on from the idea of Blade ever happening , and suggested that further questions about why it never happened should be asked directly of Marvel instead. "You had me under contract, they have billions of dollars, if they wanted to do the movie, we would've done the movie. So we're not doing the movie," Ali said. The same month, Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige admitted he felt like a "gigantic loser and failure" over the project's collapse .

Feige previously admitted that Blade had gone through "three or four" different incarnations, two of which were period pieces, before the studio finally settled on a modern day adaptation. "We didn't feel like, as we often do, you can have a good script and make it a great script through production," Feige said. "We didn't feel confident that we could do that on Blade, and we didn't want to do that to Mahershala and didn't want to do that to us."

Still, it remains surprising just how close Blade got to full production, with a full wardrobe of clothes made for the film's supporting artists, which were ultimately sold on and used for Ryan Coogler's acclaimed Sinners. Mia Goth was cast and got as far as a wig fitting , meanwhile.

The question now is, will Marvel Studios find a replacement for Ali and push forward with a new take on Blade, or give up entirely? With Ryan Gosling confirmed to be playing Ghost Rider in a new MCU movie set for release in 2028, some believe Marvel Studios is setting up the introduction of the Midnight Sons, which would potentially open the door for Blade.

In the meantime, Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother launches in theaters on September 25.

articles.title: Blizzard Insists There Are 'Many Reasons to Keep Playing' Diablo 4 as Fans Debate End of Expansions and Diablo 5 in 2029
articles.summary: Blizzard has insisted Diablo 4 still has “bright support” as the community debates the shock news that no more expansions will be released for the game and with Diablo 5 looming over the horizon.
articles.body:
Blizzard has insisted Diablo 4 still has “bright support” as the community debates the shock news that no more expansions will be released for the game and with Diablo 5 looming over the horizon.

At BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony, Blizzard announced Diablo 5 for 2029 . It’s due out six years after Diablo 4, and promises more classes than any Diablo game has had before. (If you need a catch-up, here's everything announced at BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony .)

But what does all this mean for Diablo 4? In an interview with PC Gamer , Diablo 4 game director Brent Gibson said Blizzard is now focused on releasing seasons for Diablo 4 and “getting to Diablo 5.”

“We feel like we told the Story of Hatred,” he added. “We had a great conclusion with Lord of Hatred with what we have with Mephisto, and we are moving towards telling the Story of Terror." That’s a reference to Diablo 5, which sees Diablo himself ruling over a post-apocalyptic Sanctuary.

Some Diablo 4 players have reacted to the news with anger, particularly the lack of any new expansions. Players are pointing out that former Diablo 4 boss, Rod Fergusson, mentioned “annual expansions” for the action role-playing game back in 2023 . That hasn’t happened, with just two released (Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred). Clearly, the early ambition for Diablo 4 has changed. Fergusson left Blizzard and Diablo last year to help get the new Bioshock game out the door at 2K Games.

“Why did they kill this game? I thought Lord of Hatred was well received?” one person asked on the Diablo 4 subreddit . “Guess those promises of supporting D4 for a long long time went out the window,” another said. Some are even calling into question further investment in Diablo 4, in terms of time and money.

“So why the f**k would anyone want to buy anything in D4 anymore?” another player said. “No point in buying battlepass or buying skins or collect. Unless they bring everything over to D5 like POE2, there is no point. What a disappointment.”

“This f***ing blows,” one fan added. “I thought the plan was yearly expansions, not just a 100 year timeskip and slap in the face.”

It’s important to note that others in the Diablo community are countering the backlash by saying Diablo 4 has offered — and continues to offer — plenty of content and that six years before a sequel is a reasonable amount of time.

“I spent $100 on Diablo 4 and only got over a thousand hours of entertainment,” one person joked . “Bliz bad I guess?”

“[Shrugs],” another said. “I'm not bent out of shape over the announcement, just a little surprised. As soon as you announce the next game in the series, that immediately takes the wind out of the sails of the current one. Announcing three years out, they either have a lot of faith in D4 to keep moving copies, or absolutely no faith in it.”

So, what exactly does Blizzard have in store for Diablo 4 over the next three years? At BlizzCon, it announced Season of Hell's Legacy, which starts tomorrow, September 15. Guided by the soul of the much-loved Deckard Cain, players face bosses from across the Diablo franchise, including the echoes of the Prime Evils. Further ahead, the Amazon class is coming to Diablo 4 during the first half of 2027. Just don’t expect any new expansions.

At BlizzCon, IGN spoke with Diablo 5 game director Joe Shely, narrative director Jennifer Helper, and production director Tiffany Wat, who confirmed the sequel is already in full production , but insisted there’s life left in Diablo 4.

“Diablo 4 has bright support,” Shely said. “It's fully supported by the team. We were just announcing earlier today, coming to Diablo 4, the Amazon, the Season of Hell's legacy, Diablo 4 is coming to Switch 2, and there will continue to be ongoing support for Diablo 4. There's many reasons for players to keep playing. And of course, we've been in development for some time on Diablo 5. We're in full production and it's been really an exciting time for us to be able to get to share it with players.”

Wat went on to say Blizzard has dedicated teams for each of its Diablo games, and they all work together on updates. “We have dedicated teams for each of those games because those games are important to us and they're really important for our community,” wat explained. “I think it really gives us a really great opportunity to be able to collaborate together, to talk with one another. Even though we might be distinct teams, we still work together quite closely because ultimately we are making games for the Diablo community. I think it's the best time to be a Diablo fan.”

The question for Blizzard will be whether Diablo 4 seasons and the Amazon class are enough to keep players interested. The sentinent online from core players is that Diablo 4 has, overnight, reduced interest. I've even seen some players question why they should bother fussing over the Geralt skin for the Barbarian class knowing Diablo 5 is coming in three years and cosmetics won't cross over.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: First Major Cast Member Confirms Appearance in GTA 6, Seemingly Going Off Rockstar's Script
articles.summary: The first major cast member has confirmed his appearance in Grand Theft Auto 6, seemingly going off Rockstar’s tightly controlled marketing script.
articles.body:
The first major cast member has confirmed his appearance in Grand Theft Auto 6 , seemingly going off Rockstar’s tightly controlled marketing script.

Stephen Root, who voices Bill Dauterive and Buck Strickland on the animated series King of the Hill, confirmed his involvement in GTA 6 in an interview with the Associated Press .

“Yeah, you’re gonna see me in it,” he said. “It’s coming out November 19th, is the latest I know of. I think from the first rollout of GTA they were doing maybe almost a year ago they had my character in there. And there are too many people who knew me from King of the Hill and my voice! So I think that secret kind of got divulged then.”

That’s a nod to GTA 6 Trailer 2, which featured a character who sounded so much like Root that fans put two and two together and — now we know — came up with the right answer. We know this character to be Brian Heder, a drug trafficker and apparent boatyard owner seen speaking to Jason about paying rent. “Just go get me my cheques!” he shouts as Jason heads indoors.

We see much more of Heder in the recent GTA 6 Extended Look, where he offers Jason words of advice. We also meet his wife, Lori Heder. Here’s the official blurb from Rockstar’s GTA 6 website:

“Brian's a classic drug runner from the golden age of smuggling in the Keys. Still moving product through his boat yard with his third wife, Lori, Brian's been around long enough to let others do his dirty work.

“Brian’s letting Jason live rent-free at one of his properties — so long as he helps with local shakedowns, and stops by for Lori’s sangria once in a while."

“I’m so happy to be involved with it. It’s an amazing thing to look at,” Root added when asked what it was like working on GTA 6, clearly trying not to give too much away.

Remarkably, Rockstar has yet to confirm any GTA 6 actors, leading fans to try to work out the cast for themselves. We don’t even know who plays Jason and Lucia, the game’s dual protagonists. Perhaps we won’t until the game is out in November and the credits roll.

While you wait to find out, check out IGN’s extensive GTA 6 coverage, including our interview with Rockstar’s Rob Nelson on what to expect .

articles.title: Hope: Exclusive New Images Depicting the Sci-Fi Film's Alien Intruders
articles.summary: Get an exclusive first look at director Na Hong-jin’s sci-fi thriller Hope with new images showing the film's alien invaders.
articles.body:
IGN can reveal new artwork from Hope , the new sci-fi/action film from director Na Hong-jin (The Wailing).

These images, which can be seen by scrolling through the slideshow below, features concept art created by Parallax Studios depicting the extraterrestrial creatures that crash-land on Earth in the forest outside the idyllic hamlet of Hope Harbor.

With different classes and species of otherworldly creatures now on the loose, it’s up to the chief of police, his gun-toting female sergeant, and a motley group of hunters to stop them.

IGN raved about Hope when it premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. Our critic Siddhant Adlakha awarded the film a score of 9/10, writing in his Hope review :

“Through forests, mountainsides, and claustrophobic main streets, Hope launches a gonzo sensory assault with an action-comedy-thriller saga of a small town beset by forces much larger than itself. Beginning with a lengthy climax, then unspooling a mystery in reverse before climaxing once again, its peculiar structure is as uncannily inviting as its malformed creature designs, which work to bring cultural paranoia into a riveting clash with nature.”

Adlakha continued, “It’s a nonstop blast with the kind of low-to-the-ground vehicular and horseback action that’ll have you falling off the front of your seat.”

The cast of Hope includes Hwang Junh-Min, Zo In-Sung, Hoyeon Taylor Russell, Cameron Britton, Alicia Vikander, and Michael Fassbender.

Hope opened in approximately 1,500 theaters across the U.S. on September 9. That makes it the widest domestic theatrical release for a Korean-language film since the Oscar-winning Parasite.

articles.summary: Nintendo's 'Customer Appreciation Sale', partly funded by US "Tariff Refunds", is now live with up to 30% off Switch games, memory cards, amiibo, and more.
articles.body:
Nintendo's 'Customer Appreciation Sale' is now live , limited to the United States . The sale is offering up to 30% off dozens of Switch games, accessories, amiibo, merch, and plenty more.

I'll include some of my top picks just below, but be sure to check out the full sale yourself as well in case there's anything I miss that you're particularly keen on.

$10 Nintendo eShop Gift Card (Digital Code)

Nintendo Switch 2 + Super Mario Galaxy 1&2 Bundle

Standouts in the sale include Metroid Dread, down to $41.97 after its highly anticipated sequel, Metroid Ravenous , was revealed during the recent Nintendo Direct .

There's also Resident Evil Requiem for Nintendo Switch 2 , down to its lowest price yet at $49.99. Note that this is for the boxed copy from Amazon, which includes a 'game key card'.

There are also discounts on the Nintendo Switch 2 Camera, down to $37.99 , and amiibo, such as the Metroid Prime 4: Beyond collection, now available from just $20.97 each.

Major US retailers like Amazon, alongside the Nintendo eShop, are offering the vast majority of the deals on offer in the sale. But a quick piece of advice?

If you're buying anything from Nintendo, pick up some discounted eShop gift cards from Amazon, Costco, Newegg, or wherever else first. This will ensure you're getting the best possible deal on any of your purchases.

For example, $10 Nintendo eShop gift cards are down to $8.98 at Amazon right now (see the price in the cart). While it's just over $1 in savings, that soon adds up, and if you aren't taking advantage of this while still making, you're basically throwing money away.

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 (Digital)

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom (Digital)

As I already mentioned, Metroid Dread will no doubt be at the top of many Nintendo fans lists to play after that electric Nintendo Direct trailer for Ravenous. The sequel has certainly jumped to my most anticipated game of next year as well, especially with how much I loved Dread already.

But, there are a couple of other Metroid games to check out in the sale as well. That includes Metroid Prime Remastered for $27.97 , and Metroid Prime 4: Beyond for $41.99 .

Other highlights in the sale include Super Mario Galaxy 1+2 for $48.97, Super Mario Bros. Wonder for $41.97, and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom for $48.97.

Note, that while these are all digital purchases for Nintendo Switch, you can play these on Nintendo Switch 2. But if you want to take full advantage of the new console, such as with Metroid Prime 4 or Tears of the Kingdom, you'll still need to buy the upgrade pack for around $10 as well.

Nintendo Switch 2 Deals and Preorder Discounts

Looking for the best Nintendo Switch 2 deal right now? That can be found via Walmart, where you can get a Switch 2 console + Super Mario Galaxy 1&2 for $519 .

Switch 2 consoles now cost $499.99 , so you're saving $70 in total from the MSRP of buying both separately, or around $30 total savings if you were picking up the game in the sale right now for $48.97, as I mentioned just above.

Other notable Switch 2 deals right now include, as I mentioned, Resident Evil Requiem for $49.99. While I also wanted to give a nod to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , which is down to $59.88 for a physical copy at Amazon , or $49.88 at Walmart if you get lucky with a hidden promo code .

There's also $10 off Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave at Amazon if you preorder right now. While neither of these preorder deals are limited to the Customer Appreciation Sale, they are still tremendous offers and worth mentioning for those savvy Nintendo fans out there looking to save as much as possible on their favorite hobby.

Talking of Nintendo Switch 2, Walmart also has some of the best prices we've seen on Switch 2 memory cards right now as part of the sale. The Onn 512GB MicroSD Express Memory Card is available for $84.77, while the 256GB model is $46.77, with free shipping on both.

Even better, there's an unadvertised $10 off coupon code, SAVE3X , which knocks another $10 off either card. That brings the 512GB model down to $74.77 and the 256GB card to just $36.77 .

Other notable deals in the sale include a discount on several amiibo, such as from Metroid Prime 4 or The Legend of Zelda Tears of the Kingdom. There's also Switch Joy-Con Controllers down to $62.97, sold out at Nintendo but available at Walmart (for now at least), and the Nintendo Sound Clock 'Alarmo'.

Nintendo Sale Made Possible by Tariff Refunds in the US

As a reminder, upon announcing this sale last week , Nintendo also said that it's parly being funded and made possible thanks to "tariff-related refunds." The video game giant said it "absorbed most tariff-related costs," but the refunds have helped make promotions such as this new sale possible.

Nintendo previously faced questions over what it would do with money returned after the US tariff regime was challenged. Nintendo recently raised the prices of some Switch products globally, citing a combination of factors including tariffs, rising component costs, labor and shipping.

It subsequently argued that consumers were not entitled to refunds for purchases made at those higher prices after a court ruled the tariffs illegal. Nintendo said customers had received "exactly what they bargained and paid for" and that it was not required to retroactively adjust prices following the outcome of the tariff litigation.

articles.title: Remembering Nintendo GameCube, 25 Years On From Launch
articles.summary: Today marks 25 years since the launch of Nintendo GameCube, a console that provided one of the company's most joyous eras of console gaming — even if it felt underappreciated at the time.
articles.body:
Today marks 25 years since the launch of Nintendo GameCube, a console that provided one of the company's most joyous eras of console gaming — even if it felt underappreciated at the time.

Just at a glance, the GameCube looked fun . Maybe it was the handle (did Nintendo really think we'd take it out to the shops?) or the purple-colored case. Either way, it was immediately obvious that the GameCube was designed around Nintendo's biggest strength: games that bring a smile to your face, of a kind you won't find anywhere else.

As Sony and Microsoft sought to provide DVD and CD playback, Nintendo's box focused solely on games — to the extent that it only fit mini-DVDs in its dinky disc bay. The console's front prominently advertised its capability of supporting four controllers with no extra add-ons, perfect for multiplayer games of Mario Kart: Double Dash!!, while its colourful pad remains beloved (and still used) by Nintendo fans today.

Of course, the GameCube is best remembered for its game lineup, and as the birthplace of franchises that have since become Nintendo staples. Even at release, the GameCube offered perhaps one of the best console launch lineups of all time. On arrival in Japan, on September 14, 2021, the GameCube boasted Luigi's Mansion, Wave Race: Blue Storm and Pikmin from Nintendo itself, plus Sega's brilliant Super Monkey Ball. By the time GameCube rolled out in the U.S. and Europe, that lineup was extended to include Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 and Star Wars Rogue Squadron 2: Rogue Leader, whose visuals made me feel like I was actually inside a Star Wars film.

Through the GameCube's first year, the hits kept coming. While not the first entry in the series, Super Smash Bros. Melee set the standard for Nintendo's hugely popular fighting game series. And while a version of Animal Crossing may have had a limited release on N64, its GameCube arrival built the foundations of another core franchise (even if its debut outside Japan was much delayed).

While Nintendo has never lost its eye for the unexpected, GameCube felt like a breeding ground for the company's creativity. From the terrain-shaping god game Doshin the Giant to the microphone-controlled feudal pinball game Odama, not to mention Donkey Konga's brilliant bongo drums, Nintendo published some truly bizarre — but always fun — experimental titles. (Though, sadly, some were deemed too odd for worldwide release, such as Cubivore and Giftpia.)

Alas, as time went on and the GameCube's sales numbers couldn't match PS2 or Xbox, third-party support for the console began to wane. Still, Nintendo rewarded its faithful with games that still regularly feature among lists of the all-time greats: Metroid Prime and its underappreciated sequel, Super Mario Sunshine, and The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker. And some notable third-party support did continue, with a post-Dreamcast era Sega providing the phenomenal Skies of Arcadia Legends, while the infamous Capcom 5 agreement saw the launch of the masterpiece that is Resident Evil 4.

In terms of pure numbers, GameCube was something of a failure. It shifted 21.74 million units worldwide, a figure that trailed far behind the PS2, and which Switch 2 has now eclipsed just in its first year. (The only Nintendo console to ever sell less was Wii U.) But its contribution to the history of Nintendo and its gaming library remains remarkable nonetheless. Last night I dipped back into Super Mario Sunshine via Nintendo Switch Online, and took Mario for a nostalgic dash around the rooftops of Delphino Plaza, my view out into the distance artfully blurred by a shimmering heat have. Even a quarter of a century on, there's something remarkable about Nintendo's creation — and the dinky purple box it first launched on.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Ubisoft Has Delayed Rayman Legends Retold Just a Few Weeks Before Its Planned Release Date
articles.summary: Ubisoft has delayed Rayman Legends Retold from October to December.
articles.body:
Ubisoft has delayed Rayman Legends Retold from October to December.

Ubisoft confirmed the news via a social post today, noting that although Rayman Legends Retold has gone gold and was due out October 1, it isn't quite ready for launch. The team is taking the extra time to polish the game for release, which is now set for December 3. Expect a new look next week on September 22.

This will push Rayman Legends Retold out of the blast zone of major, earthshattering releases like Gears of War, Call of Duty, and GTA 6. Of course, Rayman appeals to a whole different audience, so those games may not have impacted its release in the first place, but it does allow it to soak up a bit more attention. Placing it in the heart of the holiday season may also give it more visibility for potential gifts, but we'll have to see how it all shakes out.

Rayman Legends Retold was announced earlier this summer, and the first previews for it were quite glowing . It's a reimagining of the 2013 platformer Rayman Legends, adding all kinds of new content, gameplay features, new 3D graphics, and much more. It is, by and large, a new game that leans on elements from the original release. It is the first Rayman game in 13 years so there's hope from fans that if this performs well, the franchise will live on and continue to thrive.

Ubisoft has been on a kick of remakes this year, with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and now Rayman Legends Retold. The publisher was also supposed to release a remake of Prince of Persia: Sands of Time, but it was canceled after quality concerns and years of troubles . It seems likely that Ubisoft will continue to remake classic titles from its past following the success of Black Flag Resynced.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: LEGO Is Officially Retiring the First Harry Potter Book Nook
articles.body:
LEGO revealed its first set of book nooks back in June 2025. There were only three builds available at the time, all of which have been quite popular since their debut. Now in 2026 there are more LEGO book nooks and bookends than ever before and one of the originals is officially up for retirement.

The Hogwarts Express book nook has just been added to LEGO's 'Retiring Soon' page, marking the inevitable end of its widespread availability. It's still discounted at Amazon right now, so if you've been thinking about picking one up as a Harry Potter gift for you or a loved one, now is the time to do so.

LEGO Harry Potter Book Nook: Hogwarts Express

Although traditional book nooks are meant to be displayed between books, this Hogwarts Express build has a few different ways of being used once you put it together. You can choose to use the two sides of the set as a pair of bookends or fold them to fit neatly between books on a shelf. Both options reveal different aspects of Platform 9 and 3/4 and the train itself. As far as book nooks go, it's a bit on the smaller side with only 832 pieces included. You also get minifigures of both Harry Potter and Ron as they were in their first year at Hogwarts.

One important note is that the book nook itself is only 6.5 inches tall. This height is generally fine for most paperbacks and smaller hardcovers, but if you have taller books in your collection it might look a little bit weird. For example, the Harry Potter illustrated books are about 11 inches tall and would absolutely tower over this set on a shelf.

While this was the first official Harry Potter book nook, it isn't the only one you can buy anymore. As of June 2026 , there is also the Dumbledore's Office Book Nook. LEGO Recently Announced Its Biggest Book Nook

LEGO's line of book nooks have been entirely tied to popular franchises up until now, but that's about to change on October 1. The plastic brick company recently revealed the LEGO Bookstore Book Nook , which is made up of a whopping 1,690 pieces. This is the largest and most expensive LEGO book nook we've seen so far.
